To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the supply of N from belowground residues, including rhizo- and root exudates, to a following crop of wheat is an important component of the supply of N, but that the N derived from this pool is not included in studies using 15N approaches.
belowground residue N, including root exudates, is a major source of N to succeeding wheat crops, and that this supply is greater from pea than from canola.

the amount of N supplied to wheat from preceding crops of pea or canola was relatively small, with a larger proportion of N derived from belowground residue compared to aboveground residue, and the recovery of N from the belowground pool was higher than that from the aboveground residue pool.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more holistic understanding of the fate of N from crop residues and its contribution to the N economy in cropping systems.
the fate of N in the soil-plant system and the role that N management plays in the sustainability of crop production systems.
the supply of N from crop residues to subsequent crops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the N from aboveground crop residues was less available for wheat than the N from belowground residues, and the N from below-ground crop residues was less than half of the total N supplied from both above and belowground crop residue pools.
N from belowground residues, including rhizo-deposits, is a major component of total residue-derived N in the soil-plant system.
belowground N is important and should be included in studies of residue-derived N in subsequent crops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the supply of residue N to wheat is more important from belowground than aboveground crop residues and is more important from pea than canola.
the belowground N from the pea and canola residue was more important to the N supply to the wheat than the aboveground residue N.
belowground residues, including rhizo-deposits, can provide a significant source of N to succeeding cereal crops, and that the contribution of belowground N to N supply is species-dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N from belowground residues is often not included when estimating the N supplied to succeeding crops from residue N.
belowground residue N is an important component of N supplied from crop residues to succeeding crops and that this component is often not accounted for in 15N approaches that trace residue-derived N.
belowground N is important and should be considered in residue management studies that use 14N or 15N approaches.
